title: Online Stock Span
prompt:
Design an algorithm that collects daily price quotes for a stock and returns the span of that stock's price for the current day. The span is the maximum number of consecutive days (starting from today and going backward) for which the stock price was less than or equal to today's price.

You'll implement this as a single function `run_stock_span(prices)`, where `prices` is the sequence of daily prices fed in order via repeated `next(price)` calls on a `StockSpanner`. Return an array where the `i`-th element is the span returned immediately after feeding `prices[i]`.

examples.explanation: Day 5 (75): the previous prices 60,70,60 are all <= 75 (plus itself), so span 4. Day 6 (85): all previous prices are <= 85, so span 6.

hints: Recomputing the span by scanning backward through all previous prices for every new price gives O(n^2) in the worst case.
Keep a stack of (price, span) pairs representing prices that haven't yet been 'absorbed' by a later, bigger-or-equal price.

When a new price arrives, pop and merge every stack entry whose price is <= the new price, accumulating their spans into the new entry's span before pushing it — amortized O(1) per call since each entry is pushed and popped at most once.

solution.approach: Maintain a stack of (price, span) pairs. For each new price, initialize its span to 1, then repeatedly pop entries from the stack whose price is <= the new price, adding their span to the running total each time (since all the days they represent are also <= the new price, transitively). Push the new (price, span) pair. This amortizes to O(1) per call because each entry is pushed once and popped at most once across the whole sequence.
